speaker: john_heminges
text: Easter term ends today. The gowns go. I have put the almanac on the chest, where we can all see June.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: It is open at the week. I can see Sunday from where I am standing.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Whitsun is Sunday. I want the comedy for the Monday holiday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You can have it. The comedy. Monday the ninth.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Give me the long one again before then, the speech at the end, so I am not finding it in the yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have had it. You will have it in the morning, on the ninth, and not in the yard.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And a jig after, or a holiday yard will invent one. They invent things when the play lets them go.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Three weeks from that Monday to Midsummer. The old stock will cover it, if we mean to spend the old stock.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Three weeks. The old plays. Nothing new promised into them. Then we are at the autumn.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The— the people liked the Labour's Lost. Give me a Labour's Won for Michaelmas, Will, with the same four and the weddings in it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have a king.

speaker: john_heminges
text: How near?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He's about to be unkinged.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Michaelmas, then, when the Inns are back to hear it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Michaelmas is a long way from a Monday holiday. I want the ninth written down before anyone spends the autumn.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The ninth is settled. The comedy they already like. I am not writing a second one.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A second one with weddings would at least end where a man can dance. A king being unkinged is a long afternoon.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Let the autumn wait a quarter of an hour. I have a question, and I would rather ask it while the almanac is still open.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Ask it when we sit again. We have the Monday, and we have the three weeks. The chest can hold that much while we breathe.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The three weeks I can play. I will play them awake. I have said nothing against the ninth.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: And the holiday is the ninth, not this coming Sunday. This coming Sunday is the church, and the play is the day after.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Monday the ninth. Put it on the sheet if you do not trust the talking.

speaker: john_heminges
text: I trust a sheet. The rest of the questions are still on the almanac. They can wait a quarter of an hour, and they will not become smaller for waiting.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Three weeks, and the ninth. I can hold those two, and I would still rather the book stayed where it is.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Leave it open a moment. I can see the ninth from here, and I want to go on seeing it.
